title: Protect the main branch with rules
summary: Repository rules can require reviews or status checks before a branch accepts changes. This helps a team apply the same process consistently.
introduction: Repository rules can require reviews or status checks before a branch accepts changes. This helps a team apply the same process consistently. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain protect the main branch with rules
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Repository rules can require reviews or status checks before a branch accepts changes. This helps a team apply the same process consistently.

blocks.code:
Worked rule plan for main:
Require a pull request
Require the test status check
Require a suitable review
Allow only intended people to bypass rules
blocks.title: Protect the main branch with rules

blocks.text: The plan records a review process. Available settings depend on the repository and GitHub plan; no rule is changed by reading this lesson.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain why a broad bypass permission can weaken the plan.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A rule only helps when it is configured for the intended branch and used consistently.
For more detail later, use this [GitHub further reading](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started).
